policy: The owner's crossover rank order, with the role type each character takes in the village. Ranks, display names and assetIds are a verbatim mirror of the private corpus's selected-roster.json (sha256 below); `id` comes from scripts/crossover/build-character.py's build manifests. `kind` is docs/crossover-family-split.md's 30 Family / 133 Fellows split. `roleType` is docs/crossover-storyline-plan.md section 5.1 applied by role; `type` is that after the owner's decision 3 (spread the top picks), and the five rows that differ carry `typeMoved` with the reason. Text is written for Everkai: no franchise plot is retold here.
localNumbers: Every `type` and every line of text in this file is LOCAL -- a choice, not a measurement. The earnings consequence of a type IS measured (docs/crossover-storyline-plan.md section 5.2); which character gets which type is taste.

source.corpus: the owner's private MSF/SWGOH asset corpus, not in this repo

characters.title: Friendly Neighborhood Hero
characters.description: A quick-witted wall-crawler who dropped into the village through a tear in the sky. He patrols the rooftops at dusk, trades jokes for directions, and never walks past someone who needs a hand.

characters.typeMoved: a loner who works alone and leaves before he is thanked
characters.title: The Quiet Trapper
characters.description: Splits firewood before dawn and leaves a stack at whichever door needs it, then goes before anyone can thank him.

characters.typeMoved: a drill instructor, which is teaching
characters.title: Drillyard Steward
characters.description: Runs the morning drill on the green and will not let a recruit go home until their stance is right.

characters.title: The Lamp Wright
characters.description: Rebuilt the village water pump in an afternoon and has been improving it, loudly, ever since.

characters.typeMoved: the steadfast: hauls stone and mends the wall
characters.title: The Wall Mender
characters.description: Carries the stones two carts could not, then sits out the afternoon in the shade of the wall he raised.

characters.typeMoved: a figurehead who calls the harvest crews in
characters.title: Stormwatch Captain
characters.description: Reads the sky for the harvest crews and calls the fields in before the first drop lands.

characters.title: The Tower Tenant
characters.description: Took the empty tower, filled it with ledgers, and answers questions only when the question is precise.

characters.title: The Iron Marshal
characters.description: Keeps the foundry iron moving and speaks for the smiths whenever the village argues about wages.

characters.title: The Fallow Keeper
characters.description: Thins the orchard without sentiment, and the trees he leaves standing carry twice the fruit.

characters.title: The Doorway Scholar
characters.description: Maps the paths that shift between the hills and posts a fresh chart at the crossroads each week.

characters.title: The Kind Ear
characters.description: Sits with anyone who cannot sleep, and remembers every name in the village including the ones nobody says.

characters.title: The Ember Dancer
characters.description: Tends the pottery kiln at its hottest hour, when nobody else will stand near it.

characters.title: The Story Broker
characters.description: Sells stories at the market, and one of them is always true, though never the one you paid for.

characters.title: The Hearth Warder
characters.description: Hangs charms over the doors of new houses and will not explain what they are for.

characters.title: The Border Steward
characters.description: Walks the boundary stones every dawn and settles land disputes before they reach the elder.

characters.title: The Loud Neighbour
characters.description: Takes any job nobody wants, finishes it oddly well, and narrates the whole thing to whoever is nearby.

characters.title: The Bridge Fitter
characters.description: Measures everything twice, builds once, and has already drawn a better bridge than the one he just finished.

characters.title: The School Founder
characters.description: Opened a classroom in the old grain store and teaches whoever turns up, at whatever hour they can come.

characters.title: The Long Traveller
characters.description: Rides ahead of the trade road and comes back with news a week before the couriers do.

characters.title: The Head of Watch
characters.description: Sets the watch rota and takes the coldest shift himself without mentioning it.

characters.title: The Rain Caller
characters.description: Knows the week's weather before the sky shows it, and has never yet been wrong about a harvest.

characters.title: The Night Listener
characters.description: Walks the lanes after dark and hears trouble two streets before it starts.

characters.title: The Quiet Steady
characters.description: Steps between two arguing neighbours, and somehow both go home thinking they won.

characters.title: The Quarry Hand
characters.description: Breaks stone all morning, complains about it all afternoon, and is back at the face before sunrise.

characters.title: The Hungry Neighbour
characters.description: Guards the village larder with unsettling devotion, and eats rather more of it than he admits.

characters.title: The High Flyer
characters.description: Carries urgent post over the ridge in an hour, a trip the road takes two days to make.

characters.title: The Hearth Lighter
characters.description: Lights every forge and oven in the village before breakfast and treats it as a personal contest.

characters.title: The Ledger Keeper
characters.description: Knows who owes what to whom, and tells the elder only the parts that matter.

characters.title: The Many-Handed
characters.description: Repaired the mill gearing with four wrenches at once and will not let anyone else touch it.

characters.title: The Rooftop Menace
characters.description: Makes kites the children adore and the watch dislikes, and flies them where he should not.

characters.title: The Debt Collector
characters.description: Recovers what was stolen, returns it to the door it came from, and never stays for the thanks.

characters.title: The Careful Guest
characters.description: Arrives at a negotiation already knowing what the other side means to ask for.

characters.title: The Harbour Lord
characters.description: Runs the village water channels and reminds everyone, often, whose water it is.

characters.title: The Tune Trader
characters.description: Guides caravans over the pass and insists the whole crew sing on the climb.

characters.title: The Small Surveyor
characters.description: Keeps the hives and can tell you the state of every comb without opening a single one.

characters.title: The Dusk Warden
characters.description: Takes the shift between midnight and dawn, the one nobody else volunteers for twice.

characters.title: The Sharp Gardener
characters.description: Grows the difficult plants the apothecary needs and labels every pot twice.

characters.title: The Gadget Hand
characters.description: Fixes anything with a spring in it, charges too much, and is worth it.

characters.title: The Careful Touch
characters.description: Calms every horse in the village, and wears gloves for reasons she has not explained.

characters.title: The Morning Form
characters.description: Runs the dawn training in the square and pairs the clumsiest recruit with himself.

characters.title: The Orchard Keeper
characters.description: Planted the lane of saplings by the school and waters them without being asked.

characters.title: The Steady Aim
characters.description: Makes arrows for the archery range and quietly outshoots everyone who buys them.

characters.title: The Sleepless
characters.description: Delivers the post at hours nobody asked for, and remembers none of it in the morning.

characters.title: The Reading Room
characters.description: Catalogued the whole reading room in a week and talks with anyone who takes a book out.

characters.title: The Card Sharp
characters.description: Runs a card table at the market with terrible luck for everyone but himself.

characters.title: The Road Warden
characters.description: Patrols the night road and turns back whatever should not be on it.

characters.title: The Big Landlord
characters.description: Owns half the roofs on the lane and is unfailingly polite about the rent.

characters.title: The Bright Helper
characters.description: Volunteers for every village job at once and has not yet run out of enthusiasm.

characters.title: The Village Advocate
characters.description: Hears disputes in the square and settles them with a clarity nobody dares appeal.

characters.title: The Clock Mind
characters.description: Keeps the village clock true to the second and rings it himself when the rope frays.

characters.title: The Late Arrival
characters.description: Turned up fully grown with no history and an unnerving talent for saying the useful thing.

characters.title: The Cold Manner
characters.description: Teaches the village children to hold a conversation, and their parents to hold their tempers.

characters.title: The Borrowed Face
characters.description: Stands in for whoever is ill, in any role, and nobody notices until the play ends.

characters.title: The Chapel Step
characters.description: Rings the chapel bell on time from wherever he happens to be standing.

characters.title: The Long Memory
characters.description: Keeps the watch gear sharp and oiled, and says less about where he learned to.

characters.title: The Late Warning
characters.description: Rides in with warnings that always turn out to have been worth listening to.

characters.title: The Iron Back
characters.description: Carries roof beams up the ladder alone and apologises for taking the easy job.

characters.title: The Stopped Cart
characters.description: Shifts loaded carts out of the mud by himself, then charges for the favour.

characters.title: The Cold Study
characters.description: Runs the clinic's back room, keeps immaculate notes, and unsettles the patients he cures.

characters.title: The Short Errand
characters.description: Finishes the whole morning's errands before the market has finished opening.

characters.title: The Open Door
characters.description: Keeps the guest house, and has never once been locked out of anywhere.

characters.title: The New Watch
characters.description: Took the rooftop round nobody wanted and is better at it than anyone expected.

characters.title: The Silent Elder
characters.description: Presides over meetings without saying a word, and the meetings go faster for it.

characters.title: The Grave Warden
characters.description: Tends the village graves, keeps the records, and is kinder at a funeral than anywhere else.

characters.title: The Steady Wall
characters.description: Keeps the inn quiet with a look, and keeps the kitchen open for late arrivals.

characters.title: The Young Patrol
characters.description: Flies the ridge patrol and takes every extra shift he is offered.

characters.title: The Sharp Calm
characters.description: Teaches the blade slowly, and can name your next mistake before you make it.

characters.title: The Bright Spark
characters.description: Runs the festival lights and has not yet met a celebration she could not improve.

characters.title: The Bright Shadow
characters.description: Stands the highest watch, and asks the elder each week whether he is still wanted there.

characters.title: The Light Fingers
characters.description: Fits the village locks, tests them herself, and reports every one she beats.

characters.title: The Blunt Question
characters.description: Finds what the village has lost, charges plainly, and does not soften the answer.

characters.title: The Tracker
characters.description: Tracks what takes the livestock and comes back with it, or with the reason.

characters.title: The Old Warning
characters.description: Drills the watch as if the worst night is already scheduled, because he has seen one.

characters.title: The Old Neighbour
characters.description: Lives at the end of the lane, sells remedies that work, and is not to be underestimated.

characters.title: The Plain Speaker
characters.description: Says exactly what he means, which the market has decided to find refreshing.

characters.title: The Second Rooftop
characters.description: Shares the rooftop round, keeps her own hours, and beats the bell home every time.

characters.title: The Old Rite
characters.description: Keeps the village's oldest ceremonies, and insists they be done properly or not at all.

characters.title: The Straight Line
characters.description: Goes from here to there by the shortest route in the world, whatever is in the way.

characters.title: The Second Arrow
characters.description: Runs the archery range, keeps the scorebook, and is always one point off the record.

characters.title: The Long Council
characters.description: Chairs the difficult meetings and has never yet lost the room.

characters.title: The Short Answer
characters.description: Patrols the treeline alone, reports in three words, and misses nothing.

characters.title: The Steady Clerk
characters.description: Keeps the village's paperwork in order and quietly keeps the village in order with it.

characters.title: The Live Wire
characters.description: Lights the lane lamps without a taper, and has been asked repeatedly not to show off.

characters.title: The Cellar Door
characters.description: Minds the old cellar door nobody else will go near, and knows what is behind it.

characters.title: The Gentle Hand
characters.description: Grows the calming herbs and knows, before you speak, which one you came for.

characters.title: The Cold Count
characters.description: Counts the stores twice a week and has never been out by a single sack.

characters.title: The Old Standard
characters.description: Carries the village standard at festivals and drills the watch the rest of the year.

characters.title: The Dry Remark
characters.description: Scouts the far road, reports accurately, and makes the reporting funnier than it needs to be.

characters.title: The Duty Roster
characters.description: Writes the roster everyone complains about and nobody can improve.

characters.title: The Quiet Post
characters.description: Carries the letters that must not be read on the way, and never has been.

characters.title: The Long Patience
characters.description: Restores the old stonework a hand's width at a time and expects to finish in her own good time.

characters.title: The Small Light
characters.description: Keeps a lantern burning at the crossroads for whoever is still walking home.

characters.title: The Bright Study
characters.description: Copies the village records after school and has started correcting them.

characters.title: The Second Look
characters.description: Checks the things everyone has already checked, and finds what was missed.

characters.title: The Old Guard
characters.description: Teaches the spear to anyone who asks and remembers wars the village has no records of.

characters.title: Duel's End
characters.description: An armored warlord who arrived with his helmet cracked open from a fight long past. Villagers keep their distance, yet he lights the watchtower every night and says little about the road that led him here.

characters.title: The Steady Voice
characters.description: Speaks for the village to every visiting official and has never come back with a worse deal than she left with.

characters.title: The Quick Blade
characters.description: Teaches the sword too fast for most students and stays late with the ones who keep up.

characters.title: The New Standard
characters.description: Took command of the watch young, and the watch decided within a week that it was fine.

characters.title: The Short Cut
characters.description: Knows a faster road than the one on the map and is right about it more often than not.

characters.typeMoved: a training master for the youngest recruits
characters.title: The Patient Teacher
characters.description: Trains the village's youngest recruits and refuses to let one of them quit early.

characters.title: The Smiling Counsel
characters.description: Advises the elder with immaculate courtesy, and the advice is always good for somebody.

characters.title: The Long Shadow
characters.description: Turned up when the elder was ill and has been indispensable in a way nobody likes.

characters.title: The Old Lesson
characters.description: Teaches patience to children and to adults, and has more success with the children.

characters.title: The Little Engine
characters.description: Maintains the well pumps, whistles while doing it, and has never let one fail.

characters.title: The Small Master
characters.description: Teaches the slow lessons in the garden and is older than the village records.

characters.title: The Strong Hand
characters.description: Raises roof frames single-handed and takes payment in bread.

characters.title: The Polite Clerk
characters.description: Translates for every visiting trader and apologises constantly for their manners.

characters.title: The Fair Hearing
characters.description: Hears both sides fully before she says a word, which is why both sides ask for her.

characters.title: The Hard Practice
characters.description: Trains alone, hard, at the far end of the yard, and is civil to anyone who joins him.

characters.title: The Scrap Finder
characters.description: Brings back the broken things nobody wanted and makes half of them work again.

characters.title: The Old Grudge
characters.description: Lives above the quarry, comes down for salt, and is best left to his own arrangements.

characters.title: The Split Temper
characters.description: Fights at the festival bouts, wins, and is never once satisfied about it.

characters.title: The Cold Plan
characters.description: Has already worked out how the village fails, and told the elder, politely, in writing.

characters.title: The Two Names
characters.description: Came back from a long road with two sets of notes and will not say which is his.

characters.title: The Late Turn
characters.description: Joined the watch late, works the hardest shifts, and is still proving something.

characters.title: The Fixed Price
characters.description: Recovers strays and stolen goods for a stated fee, paid in advance, no negotiation.

characters.title: The Fat Ledger
characters.description: Owns the market stalls, rules them from a couch, and knows every debt on the square.

characters.title: The Last Word
characters.description: Hears a case once, rules once, and has never been asked to rule twice.

characters.title: The Slow Road
characters.description: Teaches by walking the fields with a student until the student works it out.

characters.title: The Kept Word
characters.description: Escorts whoever needs escorting, says almost nothing, and has never lost a charge.

characters.title: The Fine Manner
characters.description: Teaches the elegant forms, charges properly for them, and looks down on the cheap ones.

characters.title: The Four Arms
characters.description: Enters every festival bout, wins several at once, and coughs through the victory speech.

characters.title: The Smooth Deal
characters.description: Sells the village's surplus for more than it is worth and everyone leaves happy.

characters.title: The Heavy Hand
characters.description: Knocks down what must come down, and is careful only about the parts that stay up.

characters.title: The Straight Line
characters.description: Runs the building works on schedule, to the day, and is disliked for it.

characters.title: The Quiet Chair
characters.description: Chairs the village council without raising her voice and finishes every meeting on time.

characters.title: The Held Banner
characters.description: Leads the watch, carries the old banner, and will not let the village forget its debts.

characters.title: The Iron Jaw
characters.description: Breaks the hardest ground on the works and never asks for the lighter tool.

characters.title: The Empty Coat
characters.description: Drifts through the village between harvests, eats little, and leaves the room colder.

characters.title: The Plain Cloak
characters.description: Comes back from the far towns with the news the couriers did not hear.

characters.title: The Hard Teacher
characters.description: Teaches the lessons nobody thanks her for, and is usually proved right later.

characters.title: The Calm Chair
characters.description: Keeps a difficult council civil and remembers what was agreed last time.

characters.title: The Old Signal
characters.description: Runs the landing stage, calls every hazard early, and is never wrong about a tide.

characters.title: The Bright Word
characters.description: Speaks at meetings with a certainty that carries the room, then checks it afterwards.

characters.title: The Young Climb
characters.description: Rigs the scaffolds and climbs the ones he does not trust himself.

characters.title: The Long Absence
characters.description: Left the village young, came back older than the years account for, and says little about it.

characters.title: The Willing Hand
characters.description: Volunteers first, learns fast, and stays behind to put the chairs away.

characters.title: The Hard Start
characters.description: Works the quarry face like a man paying something off, and never says what.

characters.title: The Sharp Bargain
characters.description: Takes the jobs the watch cannot, names her price, and keeps to the letter of it.

characters.title: The Steady Wing
characters.description: Flies the village airship, keeps it airworthy, and never leaves a crew on the ground.

characters.title: The Bright Paint
characters.description: Paints the village signs and murals, and has improved several walls without being asked.

characters.title: The Own Road
characters.description: Takes the route she chose, reports what she found, and argues about the rest later.

characters.title: The Blind Teacher
characters.description: Teaches the class without looking at it and catches every note passed along the back row.

characters.title: The Two Errands
characters.description: Delivers the village post, and something else besides, and both arrive on time.

characters.title: The Loud Morning
characters.description: Flies the ridge run, lands rough, and has the whole crew laughing about it by supper.

characters.title: The Hard Line
characters.description: Drills the militia harder than the elder approves of, and the militia keeps turning up.

characters.title: The Front Shop
characters.description: Keeps a respectable curio shop and a back room the watch has never been shown.

characters.title: The Round Helper
characters.description: Rolls the tools out to whichever crew shouted for them, and gets there first.

characters.title: The Cold Question
characters.description: Asks the questions the watch would rather not, and gets answers the watch needed.

characters.title: The Blunt Instrument
characters.description: Guards the gate exactly as instructed and describes the job with unsettling enthusiasm.

characters.title: The Wide Hat
characters.description: Comes for whoever skipped their debt, gets them, and is gone by the next morning.

characters.title: The Old Sergeant
characters.description: Drills the watch by the book he helped write, and knows every name in the ranks.

characters.title: The Cracked Man
characters.description: Fights the festival bouts held together by will, and keeps getting back up.

characters.title: The Hired Blade
characters.description: Escorts caravans for a fair rate and stays for the drink afterwards.

characters.title: The Grand Plan
characters.description: Runs the big build, takes the credit early, and somehow finishes it anyway.

characters.title: The Calm Round
characters.description: Walks the woodland round unhurried and returns with everything the village needed to know.

characters.title: The Firm Hand
characters.description: Keeps order in the tavern lane and has never had to do it twice in one night.

characters.title: The Minded Pair
characters.description: Walks the village children to school at a careful pace with one of them aboard.

characters.title: The Quiet Ward
characters.description: Works the clinic's long nights and asks the questions the physician avoids.

characters.title: The Even Hand
characters.description: Teaches the older class calmly and has never once had to raise her voice.

characters.title: The Small Crew
characters.description: A very small supervisor and a very busy crew, who between them fix everything on the lane.

characters.title: The Second Brush
characters.description: Paints alongside the sign painter after school and is catching up faster than expected.
